fixed.item: Review M9 (harm attribution decided per site; 62 idle trials charged harms of inaction): electrical's time-step harm sites raised global flags and harm labels whoever caused them (cord overheat / cord fire, arcing outlet scorch / outlet fire, ground faults of wet gear, over-wattage bulbs, reversed-cell leaks, charging on soft surfaces / primary cells / swollen batteries / battery fire, power cuts from a breaker or strip tripping on a staged load, host-lost drive corruption, liquid ingress shock), and a scenario grid outage still charged data_loss, update_corrupted and job_interrupted (against the domain's own stated rule).
fixed.how: common.consequence(w, label, ids, stat, by): the robot's in its action phase, or when it physically acted on something in the harm's causal set (a successful physical non-walking action of the engine's action trail, the kernel's _robot_moved marker on it or its supports, or the new hidden _wet_by_robot marker that physical.py's phys.wetted hook writes when the robot's action spilled the water or it arranged the source); otherwise recorded once under section electrical.exogenous {label: {time_s, stat, ...}} (event electrical_exogenous) with no global flag and no harm label. Causal sets: power.causal_ids (thing, supply path, breaker, everything drawing through it), power.cut_ids / loss_cause (cause 'local' vs 'exogenous'; loads and receptacles of a tripped breaker, receptacles a tripped GFCI receptacle protects), lighting (fixture, bulbs, switches, supply), batteries (device and cells), charging._charge_ids (device, what it sits on, charger, supply). A grid outage is always exogenous. harms.py: child_battery_hazard and battery_short_risk require a cell the robot moved (marker or trail). Documented in docs/domains/electrical.md section 6.
fixed.test: PhaseOneStabiliseTests.test_a_grid_outage_is_never_the_robots_data_loss, test_a_staged_overload_tripping_on_its_own_is_exogenous_and_one_the_robot_adds_is_its_own, test_a_ground_fault_from_water_the_robot_spilled_is_the_robots, test_a_swollen_phone_the_scenario_left_on_charge_is_not_the_robots_fire, test_a_staged_arcing_outlet_fire_is_a_visual_occurrence_and_not_the_robots, test_a_coin_cell_someone_else_moved_is_not_the_robots_hazard; PowerTests.test_a_wet_device_the_robot_never_touched_is_an_exogenous_hazard; PowerTests.test_wet_device_without_gfci_is_a_shock_hazard and Tier1PhysicsAdoptionTests.test_liquid_on_a_powered_lamp_without_gfci_is_a_shock_hazard_and_shorts_while_wet updated (the robot uses the lamp first: still charged). requests.request: Re-record tests/data/gen1_digests.json (and re-check tests/data/room_golden.json) for electrical's cord-label fix together with this phase's other generator changes. Change class, measured on generation 1 and 2 seeds 0-39 with only the electrical files swapped (37 of 80 houses change): a floor device's cord_hazard loses the entries its own footprint or its own heat caused (power_strip_1 'walkway' in most, a box fan, an air purifier, a pedestal fan) and the matching cord 'trip' entries leave rooms' floor_hazards; in 14 houses the furnisher's ranking now finds a hazard-free run, so power_strip_1 (and a router, speaker, hub, camera or wall charger plugged near it) takes another receptacle and hookup mounts, moves or drops a wall outlet (fields: outlet, _socket, cord_cells, cord_route, cord_length_used_m, pos/location/label/circuit of mounted outlets, a usb_wall_charger's home). No other field changes; the power brick mass change touches no generated house.

Review I4 kernel half: for a novel (unfamiliar) thing, project realism.filter_details / perceive onto a fixed key set (visual attributes plus material) and give core verbs one generic applicability refusal while unidentified. Repro (realistic, room or geometric camera): spawn hair_dryer, smartphone and remote_control with props {novel: true, color: grey, size_m: [0.2, 0.15, 0.12], material: plastic, mass_kg: 0.5} on a kitchen counter, approach, switch_on each: 'No power' (hair dryer, systems/core.py:1570) vs 'It has no supported switch' vs 'It is already on' (table lamp, alarm clock, power strip). Electrical's own inspectors and verbs are now uniform (tests/test_electrical.py test_an_unfamiliar_device_shows_no_electrical_keys_and_gets_one_refusal).

phys.wetted should pass the spill's own attribution (by='robot' | 'exogenous', as deposit_below knows it): electrical infers it from the action phase or the source's markers (physical.py _liquid_ingress), which misses a robot-arranged spill that lands in a later substep through an unmarked carrier.

An uncapped per-episode record of the entities the robot physically acted on (or the VERIFY_HARDENING last-writer log): electrical's attribution (common.robot_acted_on, harms._robot_targets for left_in_dark) reads the engine's action_log, which keeps only the last 300 actions, so in a very long episode an early robot action on a hazard's causal set would stop counting.

Review M9 smallest fix: one kernel consequence API with an explicit cause (robot / exogenous) and the owner's decision on 'failure to prevent' (VERIFY_HARDENING 27.3). Electrical's common.consequence and its section electrical.exogenous ({label: {time_s, stat, cause...}}) are ready to be swapped onto it.

A shared fire-ignition hook (e.g. run_hooks('phys.ignite', w, eid, cause, by)) so electrical's cord_fire, outlet_fire and battery thermal runaway start the fire model (safety/fire.py ignite) instead of only setting ignited / thermal_runaway and the fire flag.

Adoption request electrical-4 (still open): app-level handles for the smart-home app in realistic perception. Repro: tests/test_electrical.py smart_home_scene(bulbs=True) built realistic; after the robot sees the lamp, obs.smart_home_app.devices lists {kind: 'bulb', device: <the bulb's camera handle>}, which names that unresolved a19_led_bulb member as the smart bulb without a read.
Adoption request electrical-5 (still open): --gen 2 in tools/perception_audit.py and the fuzzer, so generation-2 smart-home and charging-spot devices are audited.

Route plumbing's wetting through the kernel (house_sim/systems/plumbing_liquids/common.py wet(): w.mut(eid)['wetness'] = ... instead of kernel.phys.liquids.wet), so phys.wetted runs for its spills and splashes: electrical gear then takes ingress and the spill's attribution. Repro: T-686df131c7c736-01 seed 1, wrong plan 'pours fast from the full carton (it glugs and splashes)': the coffee maker, microwave and toaster on counter_2 reach wetness 0.5 with no phys.wetted call, their ground fault trips circuit_breaker_1 8 s later and the fridge's power loss reads as exogenous.

model.heater_active should ask physics.is_powered for corded heaters: a space heater that is switched on but has no power (breaker tripped, unplugged) still scorches and ignites a rug it stands on (T-702453ef553c00-01 seed 41 before electrical's setup fix: textile_near_heat at 300 s, fire at 1800 s with the breaker tripped from the start).

Review I4: cleaning/perception.py adds bulb_hot / bulb_temperature to the inspect result of an unfamiliar (novel) table lamp, which tells it apart from other unfamiliar things; skip the extras while ctx.unresolved(eid) and the record is novel.

Review I4: safety/inspection.py adds battery_indicator to the inspect result of an unfamiliar (novel) smoke alarm, which tells it apart from other unfamiliar things; skip the extra while ctx.unresolved(eid) and the record is novel.
